intervals.label: cavity excavation
intervals.quote: Dec. 1991 The cavity excavation for the construction of the Super-Kamiokande detector started.

intervals.label: detector construction and water fill
intervals.quote: Jun. 1994 The cavity excavation was completed. The construction of the detector was started.

intervals.label: SK-I
intervals.quote: Super-Kamiokande began operation at midnight on April 1, 1996.

intervals.label: PMT implosion accident and recovery
intervals.note: History page: implosion accident Nov. 2001 damaged more than 6,777 inner-detector PMTs; recovery completed and observations restarted (at half photosensor density) in Oct. 2002.

intervals.label: SK-II (half PMT density after the 2001 accident)
intervals.quote: The observations restarted in October 2002 with half the original density of photosensors.

intervals.label: SK-III (full PMT density restored)
intervals.quote: Jun. 2006 Full reconstruction of Super-Kamiokande [...] the number of photomultiplier tubes in the inner tank is now 11,129

intervals.label: SK-IV (new front-end electronics and DAQ)
intervals.note: End date is when gadolinium loading (SK-Gd) began, per the same history page. A separate 2023 solar-neutrino paper (src:sk-prd-2024-solar) analyses an SK-IV data sample running only through May 2018; that is the cutoff of one specific analysis, not a stated end of the SK-IV hardware phase, so it is not used as the interval boundary.
intervals.quote: Replacement of front-end electronics and data acquisition system.

intervals.label: SK-Gd (gadolinium-loaded ultra-pure water)
intervals.quote: Aug. 2020 The SK-Gd Project Began With the addition of gadolinium, the upgraded Super-Kamiokande detector, known as SK-Gd, began operation.

name: Super-Kamiokande
notes: The ontology's experiment-kind enum has no value for proton decay search; recorded in physics_goals only, as with experiment:kamiokande.

physics_goals.quote: One of the main goals of the Super-Kamiokande experiment is to reveal the properties of neutrinos through observations of solar, atmospheric, and accelerator-produced neutrinos.
physics_goals.value: Reveal neutrino properties by observing solar, atmospheric and accelerator-produced neutrinos

physics_goals.quote: By detecting neutrinos from supernova explosions, we can investigate in detail how stars explode. We can also explore the history of the universe by observing neutrinos from the many supernova explosions that have occurred throughout cosmic history.
physics_goals.value: Use neutrinos to investigate stellar processes and cosmic history, including supernova and supernova-relic neutrinos

physics_goals.quote: Grand Unified Theories (GUTs), which aim to unify the fundamental forces of nature, predict that protons may decay into lighter particles. Super-Kamiokande searches for this as-yet unobserved phenomenon.
physics_goals.value: Search for proton decay predicted by Grand Unified Theories

physics_goals.locator: T2K NIM paper (arXiv:1106.1238), Section 1 Introduction; K2K tutorial page
physics_goals.note: K2K half of the value: K2K tutorial page (src:k2k-tutorial-page) says a muon neutrino beam produced at KEK-PS "will be injected to Super-Kamiokande, located 250 km west of KEK". T2K half: the quoted sentence from the T2K NIM paper (src:t2k-nim-2011).
physics_goals.quote: T2K uses Super-Kamiokande [3] as the far detector to measure neutrino rates at a distance of 295 km from the accelerator
physics_goals.value: Serve as the far detector for the K2K and T2K accelerator neutrino experiments

summary.plain: A tank of 50,000 tonnes of ultra-pure water, a kilometre under a mountain near Kamioka, watched by more than eleven thousand light sensors. It caught the first solid evidence that neutrinos change type as they travel, has watched the Sun in neutrinos for decades, and is the distant target for neutrino beams fired from J-PARC.
summary.technical: Ring-imaging water Cherenkov detector, 39.3 m diameter x 41.4 m height, 50 kt total / 22.5 kt fiducial mass, 11,129 inner 20-inch PMTs (~40% photocoverage) plus an outer veto layer. Operating since 1 April 1996 through phases SK-I to SK-IV and, from August 2020, gadolinium-loaded SK-Gd. Reported evidence for atmospheric-neutrino oscillation (PRL 81, 1562, 1998) and solar-neutrino oscillation; far detector for K2K and T2K.

unique_capabilities.note: No fetched source states this superlative directly in this wording; inferred from the detector's mass and its comparison-table position relative to Kamiokande and Hyper-Kamiokande.
unique_capabilities.value: The largest operating water Cherenkov detector until Hyper-Kamiokande, able to reconstruct neutrino direction and energy in real time
